title: Catching Edge Cases AI Misses
description: Automated coding pipelines are built to produce one confident answer per document, not to notice when two legitimate sources in the same chart contradict each other — which is exactly the edge case that needs a human.

title: The Shape of a Confident Error
description: Predict which encounters a pipeline will get wrong while reporting high confidence — why a confidence score measures pattern-match strength against training data, not clinical certainty about this patient; the specific shape of a confident error (common presentation, atypical true cause); how a note's surface phrasing can pattern-match to the wrong diagnosis independent of its clinical content; why rare diagnoses get miscoded with false confidence precisely because the training data barely contains them; and building a personal watch list of the encounter patterns most likely to fool the pipeline you work with.

title: Comorbidity and Complexity
description: Code encounters where several conditions interact and the pipeline treats them as independent — the mandatory etiology/manifestation code pairs that must travel together, telling a genuine complication from a merely coincidental co-occurring diagnosis, why a condition sitting in the history isn't automatically a condition affecting this encounter's care, and how severity and acuity modifiers carry clinical weight a pipeline defaults away from when documentation doesn't spell it out explicitly.
